title: ci-local.sh: the new input-parity gate is unreachable — both full-suite run_gates call sites still cap at 8 gates
evidence:
"Input parity (T1 across inputs — mouse == touch == controller)|tools/harness.sh input-parity"
)

  run_gates "$([ "$FAST" -eq 1 ] && echo 2 || echo 8)"
}

if [ "$IN_CONTAINER" -eq 1 ]; then
  run_gates "$([ "$FAST" -eq 1 ] && echo 2 || echo 8)"
  exit $?
detail: This fix added the 9th GATES entry and rewrote the header/usage claims to "all 9 gates" but left both run_gates counts at 8, so ${GATES[@]:0:8} never reaches the input-parity gate in --mac or --in-container mode. GH CI still runs it, so the local mirror silently loses the fix's own pin.
recommended_fix: Bump both full-suite counts to 9: run_gates "$([ "$FAST" -eq 1 ] && echo 2 || echo 9)" at lines 162 and 227 (keep --fast at 2).

title: has_key(keys[:], .Esc) is always true — unwritten key-buffer slots zero-initialize to the .Esc enum value
detail: keys is a fixed [4] array whose unwritten slots hold zero (= .Esc, the first enum member); has_key scans all four slots, so esc_pressed is computed true every frame, ESC or not. It is unread today, but any future reader silently sees always-true — the ESC gate would never work.
recommended_fix: Scan only the written prefix: if has_key(keys[:keys_n], .Esc) — matching the phase-1 emission loop, which already bounds by keys_n.
